assertions.title: Quick Actions navigate to correct panels

steps.action: Open /janus?view=all and click each of the seven Quick Action buttons from the dashboard shell
steps.expected: Each action switches to the correct workspace view and leaves the destination panel visible in the viewport
steps.observed: Create Project -> /janus?view=projects with new-project-panel top 268 / bottom 686; Import Repo -> /janus?view=pipeline with repo-import-panel top -820 / bottom -534 (outside viewport); Upload Bundle -> /janus?view=pipeline with artifact-uploads-panel top -820 / bottom -240 (outside viewport); Review Builds -> /janus?view=pipeline with builds-panel top -256 / bottom -41 (outside viewport); Create Deployment -> /janus?view=pipeline with deployments-panel top -25 / bottom 569 (partially visible); Open Endpoint -> /janus?view=pipeline with domains-panel top 585 / bottom 800; API Routes -> /janus?view=reference with api-panel top 332 / bottom 800.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed via agent-browser errors during the quick-action checks
evidence.network: Quick Actions only changed the client-side /janus?view=projects|pipeline|reference route; no backend API call was required for the navigation itself.

assertions.issues: Import Repo, Upload Bundle, and Review Builds still overscrolled past their destination panels, leaving the targets completely outside the viewport after the workspace view switched.

assertions.title: Error boundaries catch and display errors gracefully

steps.action: Create the isolated account and sign into the real dashboard auth panel from /janus?view=auth
steps.expected: The browser surface is authenticated so boundary-wrapped dashboard sections can be exercised through normal user actions
steps.observed: The auth panel successfully created frontend-hardening-ut+shells-round2-20260315@example.com and then signed in the same account, leaving the dashboard usable in a signed-in state.

steps.action: Navigate the signed-in dashboard plus the /billing and /monitoring shell routes and check whether any real user action surfaces the boundary fallback UI
steps.expected: A component-level crash reachable from the real UI renders a user-friendly fallback with retry/navigation guidance
steps.observed: No user-triggerable crash path surfaced from the dashboard or shell routes; visible text never included fallback affordances such as 'Try Again', 'Something went wrong', or the section error titles, and no blank-screen crash occurred.

evidence.consoleErrors: none observed; agent-browser errors stayed empty while exercising the signed-in dashboard and shell routes
evidence.network: The auth panel completed the real sign-up/sign-in flows for the isolated account, but no boundary-specific fallback or crash behavior was exposed afterward.

assertions.issues: Blocked because no real user-surface action exposed a component-level crash that would surface the error-boundary fallback UI.

assertions.title: Billing page renders with proper states

steps.expected: The billing route shows loading, empty, and error states around Stripe-backed billing data
steps.observed: The route renders a static Billing / Coming Soon placeholder with back-to-dashboard links only.

steps.action: Inspect the page for billing-specific shells or retry UI
steps.expected: At minimum, a loading shell, invoice empty state, or user-friendly error state is present
steps.observed: No loading indicator, invoice empty state, or error shell appeared; the page stayed on the static placeholder copy.

evidence.network: Navigating to /billing only rendered the route document; no billing-specific data shell or follow-on Stripe/invoice fetch state surfaced in the UI.

assertions.issues: The billing route exists, but it still renders only a static Coming Soon placeholder instead of the required loading, empty, and error states.

assertions.title: Monitoring page renders with proper states

steps.expected: The monitoring route shows loading, empty, and user-friendly error states for deployment metrics
steps.observed: The route renders a static Monitoring / Coming Soon placeholder with back-to-dashboard links only.

steps.action: Inspect the page for monitoring-specific shells or retry UI
steps.expected: At minimum, a loading shell, empty metrics state, or user-friendly error state is present
steps.observed: No loading indicator, empty metrics state, or error shell appeared; the page remained a static placeholder.

evidence.network: Navigating to /monitoring only rendered the route document; no monitoring/metrics loading or error UI surfaced from the page.

assertions.issues: The monitoring route exists, but it still renders only a static Coming Soon placeholder instead of the required loading, empty, and error states.

frictions.description: Quick Action validation required DOM bounding-box checks because switching from All to Pipeline reflowed the page after the click, making screenshots alone ambiguous for viewport coverage.
frictions.resolution: Recorded getBoundingClientRect() positions for each target panel and paired them with screenshots to determine whether the target remained in the viewport.

frictions.description: agent-browser get text body on these Next.js routes included streamed flight payload text after the visible page copy, which added noise while checking for fallback/placeholder text.
frictions.resolution: Used screenshots plus targeted visible-text presence checks for boundary/fallback markers instead of relying on the raw body dump alone.

blockers.description: No real user-surface action exposed a component-level crash that would surface an error-boundary fallback.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Created and signed into the isolated account, exercised the signed-in dashboard and shell routes, and explicitly checked for boundary fallback text such as 'Try Again', 'Something went wrong', or the section error titles, but no crash/fallback UI became reachable.

summary: Tested 4 assigned assertions: 3 failed (VAL-FH-012, VAL-FH-025, VAL-FH-026) and 1 was blocked (VAL-FH-021). Quick-action overscroll still affects Import Repo, Upload Bundle, and Review Builds; /billing and /monitoring still render static Coming Soon placeholders; and no real-browser crash path surfaced the error-boundary UI.
